newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Upgrade may raise investment in Argentina-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Upgrade may raise investment in Argentina-analysts.

text.p: Argentina could attract more investment after Wednesday's upgrade to the country's credit rating by Standard & Poor's, rewarding the government in its efforts to reform the economy over recent years.
Although the news was widely expected, analysts said it was noteworthy considering the credit rating agency bypassed its normal procedure of first changing the country's outlook.
Argentina's rating was upped directly to BB from BB-minus without a prior change to the "stable" outlook. The outlook remained "stable."

"There is a world of investors with investment rules that could not invest in Argentina. Therefore now there is a new group of investors that can invest here," said Esteban Thomsen, Argentina economist at ING Barings.
Following upbeat statements by S&P President Leo O'Neill three weeks ago when he announced the debt review of Argentina, analysts were sure the country was heading for an upgrade.
A recent Reuters poll found that five analysts expected an imminent upgrade with three harboring doubts only on the timing of the upgrade.

S&P said the upgrade, which puts Argentina at the same grade as Mexico, came thanks to "a six year-old political commitment to prudent fiscal and financial policies that has weathered recession and elections, and favourably distinguishes Argentina from other BB-minus rated sovereigns."

"The achievement of price stability and financial predictability anchors popular support for the convertibility plan, and makes broad policy continuity increasingly likely through future political transitions," it added.

"The rating is now only two grades below being declared fit for investment, this will imply lower debt costs and move investment could come to the country," Miguel Kiguel, Finance Undersecretary was quoted by the state news agency Telam as saying. Argentina is now two notches below investment grade.

Not only will Argentina's upgrade help investment to the country, but the upgrade of neighboring Brazil Wednesday as well could help investment to the region as a whole. S&P raised Brazil's long-term foreign currency debt rating to BB-minus from B-plus.
Analysts said this will boost the market, but in the short-term stocks and bonds could remain nervous considering last week's hike in rates by the U.S. Federal Reserve.

"In the short-term, it (the Argentine market) will depend on behaviour of the U.S. long bond," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed-income analyst at Banco Rio de la Plata. "But in the next six months, this could fuel more money to our market."
Despite the perception that this will attract more funds to Argentine assets, some questioned whether an upgrade by just one credit rating agency is enough.
The general manager of Duff & Phelp's rating agency told Reuters no modification was planned in its rating of Argentina. It rates Argentina's foreign currency debt BB.
"A more precise signal to the markets would be an upgrade by all the agencies," said Costa Bourdieu.
